articles.summary: It used to be that on a typical afternoon, my husband would send me a message asking whether he needed to grab anything for dinner on his way home from work. Ah, dinner . “What do we eat?” I would say. “Well, there’s always fajitas,” he’d suggest. “Or I guess we could do tortellini again,” I’d offer. Or maybe one of us would say, half-heartedly, that we should try something new. (Cue some Googling for easy family-dinner recipes .) On our best days, this conversation would occur midday, leaving time for a fridge check. More often, it would occur at 5:15 p.m. while I was standing on the sidelines of my kids’ swimming lesson or supervising a playground trip, straining to remember whether we already had mozzarella. articles.title: What We’re Grateful For
articles.author: The Free Press
articles.summary: This year, America celebrated 250 years since its founding. There were fireworks and parades, but of all the traditions this country has handed down, one of the best may be the one that arrives today: a day set aside, by Abraham Lincoln’s proclamation, to say thank you. This has also been a year in which much has felt uncertain—politically, technologically, economically—and everything seemed to speed up. Maybe that’s why, when we asked our Free Press staff and contributors what they’re grateful for, so many of their answers came back to slowing down and focusing on what’s right in front of us: new babies, a diner that doesn’t deliver, grandparents down the block. Others cast a much wider net and said they were grateful for a country that, at 250, still has its best days ahead of it. Before we get to the responses, we want to express our collective gratitude for you, Free Press subscribers. You make everything we do possible. stories.summary: AI is reshaping Black Friday shopping, but retailers’ growing reliance on the technology could be a blind spot in the face of AI-enabled cyberattacks. Unlike human store managers prone to slashing prices to lure shoppers, AI “ has the confidence to hold its nerve ,” a price optimization platform co-founder said. But ransomware attacks on retailers are 50% more frequent in November, and the recent surge in cyberattacks is raising concerns for a sector with low levels of cyber insurance: “Black Friday should be treated as a resilience exercise as much as a revenue opportunity,” a cyber executive said. — Mary Lawrence Ware

articles.author: Leah Quinn
articles.summary: Kenya is now a major destination for Chinese solar parts, with shipments up significantly in the first 10 months of the year. China has exported $576 million worth of solar cells to the East African country so far this year, compared to $5 million for the same period in 2025, Bloomberg reported. This coincides with a jump in panel shipments from Kenya to the US market, from almost none in January to $138 million in August, fueling speculation that Kenya provides an intermediary destination to sidestep Washington’s tariffs on Chinese imports. In November, Kenya’s government spent $35 million to steady prices at the pump until mid-December in response to spiking diesel costs due to the war in Iran; with further price volatility expected, solar provides an alternative energy source. According to a report by energy think tank Ember , 17 gigawatts of solar was installed across Africa in 2026, the equivalent of 100,000 new solar panels every day. Ember forecast that by the end of the year, African solar panel manufacturing would have quadrupled, predominantly for export, with plants also in Egypt and Tanzania. — Leah Quinn
